crime_highlights: He picked up the knife and inflicted a number of stab wounds on the victim.
The most serious of the wounds was a stab wound to the left front chest, which punctured the victim's lung.
Two persons tried to stop the accused, but he continued to attack the victim with his feet.
He threatened the victim not to tell.
The victim was taken to hospital and required surgical treatment for his chest wound.
rationale_highlights: I infer that her behaviour adversely affected her parenting of her son
the accused had a disadvantaged upbringing which had at least some causal connection to his Aboriginal background
But I find there is not much mitigating effect in this, because the nature of this crime puts it in a class where sentences should be similar for Aboriginals and non-Aboriginals.
note: Court finds little mitigating effect due to violent nature of crime.

crime_highlights: Mr. Seitcher and a Mr. Reginald David assaulted Mr. Manson during the early morning hours of August the 12th of 2001.
Mr. Manson was kicked to death.
Mr. Seitcher has admitted that he kicked Mr. Manson and stomped on Mr. Manson
She described the assault as being violent and vicious.
She noted that it had split a very close First Nations community.
rationale_highlights: Mr. Seitcher's personal circumstances as a child and as a young person were extremely difficult.
Mr. Seitcher is an Aboriginal offender.
Mr. Seitcher's difficult personal childhood and youth is one of the particular factors to which particular regard must be paid pursuant to s. 718.2(e).
note: Court never states the effect on sentence; only that particular regard must be paid.

crime_highlights: Mr. Johnny stabbed a knife into Mr. Griffin's neck, injuring his oesophagus and his jugular vein.
Mr. Griffin suffered life threatening injuries.
The offender then told Mr. Griffin that his companion had a gun, and Mr. Griffin was ordered to leave the taxi cab, which he did.
Mr. Johnny continued to drive the cab until it was disabled by a spike belt that was laid on the highway in his path of travel.
rationale_highlights: I accept that the environment in the community in which he spent many of his formative years was problematic, and has probably had a negative influence on his upbringing.
the goals of denunciation and deterrence overtake the mitigating effects of the offender's aboriginal background
I have concluded that the offender's aboriginal origins are a factor that should serve to reduce what might otherwise be his sentence for this offence
note: Reduction applied only to the consecutive evasion sentence, not the robbery.
